description:
First entry with CDEMO-CU03-USR-SELECTED blank - MAIN-PARA's non-REENTER branch at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:95-105, which is the screen paint every later case re-enters from. EIBCALEN is 194, so :94 moves DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN) into CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and the IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :95 is true; the branch then does four things in source order. SET CDEMO-PGM-REENTER TO TRUE at :96, which is why the navigation pinned here carries CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1 where the request carried 0 - the next call is a re-entry and will take the :107 arm instead. MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COUSR3AO at :97. MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL at :98, which IS the cursor - COBOL positions it by moving -1 into a length item - so it is pinned as cursorField and not as a payload field. Then the guard at :99-100, which is FALSE here because CDEMO-CU03-USR-SELECTED arrived as eight spaces: the MOVE at :101-102 and the PERFORM PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :103 are both skipped, and USRSEC is never touched - no read, no read-for-update and no delete. That is asserted positively rather than by omission: expectedWrites is empty, all ten rows are pinned unchanged at indices 0-9 as their six CSUSR01Y fields and as their full 80-byte images, and expectedDatasets pins the dataset at ten rows of eighty bytes. The PERFORM SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN at :105 sits OUTSIDE the :99 IF and is therefore unconditional, which on this path yields exactly ONE send. That single-send baseline is what makes case03's third send visible, where the same unconditional statement runs again after PROCESS-ENTER-KEY has already sent twice; it is preserved behaviour and not a defect to collapse. SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN at :213-225 is the send itself: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :215 repaints the six header items, MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :217 truncates the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE into the 78-byte screen field on the right, and the SEND at :219-225 transmits COUSR3AO with ERASE and CURSOR. Eleven fields are pinned and no more, which is exactly the eleven items app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY declares as xxxI - TRNNAMEI X(4), TITLE01I X(40), CURDATEI X(8), PGMNAMEI X(8), TITLE02I X(40), CURTIMEI X(8), USRIDINI X(8), FNAMEI X(20), LNAMEI X(20), USRTYPEI X(1) and ERRMSGI X(78) - with NO password item, the one field COUSR02C's twelve has and this screen does not. The field the operator types an identifier into is USRIDIN and not USERID, which is COUSR01's spelling. They are keyed here under the xxxO names of the COUSR3AO REDEFINES at :85 onwards because the group a SEND transmits is the output group; the identities and the declared widths are the xxxI items' own. The xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items are length, flag and attribute metadata and are never payload members, which is why USRIDINL appears as the cursor and nowhere else. Four of the eleven are LOW-VALUES rather than spaces - USRIDINO, FNAMEO, LNAMEO and USRTYPEO - because :97's group MOVE writes X'00' and nothing on this path writes them again, while ERRMSGO is 78 spaces because :87 cleared WS-MESSAGE before the :90 test and no arm wrote a message into it. Both read as 'blank' and they are different bytes, and holding that distinction is a large part of why this case exists. No message text is invented. ERRMSGC is DFHDFCOL, the default-colour byte: app/bms/COUSR03.bms:140-143 declares the field COLOR=RED LENGTH=78 statically, but the program moves no colour into ERRMSGC on this path, and DFHRED plus '*' highlighting belongs to the REENTER validation arms - COUSR03C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY and sets its attributes inline. Termination is RETURN_TRANSID and not XCTL: the transaction returns to itself pseudo-conversationally with the 194-byte area carried in the payload, so no server-side session state exists and no nextProgram transfer occurs. Two message channels are pinned rather than one because the MOVE SPACES at :87-88 reaches two receivers of different widths - WS-MESSAGE at PIC X(80) and ERRMSGO at PIC X(78) - and exactly one of them, the 78-byte screen error line, is the blank error line the terminal shows; a single unchannelled line could not say which width it meant. PROVENANCE: every value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the sources named below and is NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL - running it is empirically impossible in this environment (no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler's indexed-file handler is disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository), which is the documented eight-blocker deviation escalated as risk R-A; it changes the provenance of the expected values and nothing else. Derived from app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:87-88, :94-105 and :213-225 under the pinned 2022-07-19T23:12:35 clock taken from the version footer at :358, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 (160 bytes) with the inline 05 CDEMO-CU03-INFO of app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:50-58 (34 bytes, 194 in total, including the VALUE 'N' at :54), app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22 for the two PIC X(40) titles, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the mm/dd/yy and hh:mm:ss header images POPULATE-HEADER-INFO builds at :252-262, app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy for the message field the blank line occupies, app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 (8+20+20+8+1 = 57, plus SEC-USR-FILLER's 23 = 80), app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY:24-84 for the eleven items and their widths, app/bms/COUSR03.bms for the 24x80 map they sit on, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for transaction CU03 and the USRSEC file binding, and the ten in-stream rows of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose 57-character width against the LRECL=80 RECFM=FB of :48 and the RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) of :65-66 is exactly what the declared normalisation supplies. The literal PASSWORD in SEC-USR-PWD is legacy sample data carried byte for byte because CSUSR01Y places it inside the eighty bytes; plaintext credentials are an inherited property of the legacy design rather than a choice made here, this screen has no password field and never reads or paints that span, and no hashing, encoding or token is introduced. Conventions are case01.json's, unchanged: the same ten-row seed block, the same pinned clock, the same six record field names and the same 57-to-80 normalisation.

THE OPERATION ORDER, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED. expectedOperations names every USRSEC operation this case must issue, in order, and it is an assertion a byte fingerprint structurally cannot make: the EXEC CICS DELETE at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:307-311 names no RIDFLD, so it removes the record the task is HOLDING and is only ever correct after the EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :269-278 took that hold on the same record. An empty list is equally an assertion - it says this path never reached the file at all.
